subject: general
question: Before the present premises, where did the Supreme Court of India operate from?

options.text: From the High Court of Delhi

solution:
The correct answer is __**From the parliament building**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Before **moving to its current location on Tilak Marg in New Delhi, **the Supreme Court of India operated from the old Parliament House.
 
• The **Supreme Court was inaugurated on January 28, 1950, in the Chamber of Princes in the old Parliament building**.
 
• Th**e Supreme Court operated from the old Parliament House until it moved to its current location in 1958**
 
• The Supreme Court of India can meet at any other location in addition to its permanent seat in New Delhi, if the Chief Justice of India and the President of India decide so.
 
• **This flexibility is provided under Article 130 of the Indian Constitution. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• It took the place of both the Federal Court of India and the Privy Council's Judicial Committee, which were at the time the highest courts in India.
 
• However, the first hearings and inauguration were held on January 28, 1950, at 9:45 a.m., when the judges took their seats. As a result, the date of establishment is considered official.
 
• The Supreme Court of India is India's top court and the highest judicial authority.
 
• It is the highest-ranking constitutional court with judicial review authority.
 
• The Supreme Court of India, which has a maximum of 34 judges and vast powers in the form of original, appellate, and advisory jurisdictions, is led by the Chief Justice of India.
 
• As India's supreme constitutional court, it hears appeals mostly from high courts in various states of the Union, as well as other courts and tribunals.
